### Step 0 — Configure

1. **Pre-flight.** `.bionic/` exists; `docs-root:` read from `.bionic/config.yaml` (default `.bionic/docs`) with `{specs,plans,adrs,incidents}/` present; `mkdir -p .bionic/tmp/`; both hooks installed and executable (if not, warn and record in `record/<wave>/assumptions.md`). Then probe the machine: `resources_probe` prints `cores=… mem_gb=… disk_free_gb=…`, the probe's estimate, which caps nothing. Width is the gate's, read off the machine as it is, under the share `session-poker.sh share` prints. No plan needs a `parallel-budget:` line; one marked `source=user` or `source=override` is a person's cap on writers, and it is the only cap.
2. **Classify the triple silently.** Infer from the request's verbs and named artifacts. Do NOT interrogate. Interview by exception only, 1–3 questions, on exactly three conditions: a genuine intent collision the classification rules do not resolve (the standing gray zones are **mechanism-swap** and **reference-content**); a suspected but unconfirmed security/privacy surface; or a scale that could be one session or several.
3. **Infer the flags.** `language` from repo files; `surface_type`/`has_ui` from the request; `multi_agent` defaults **true** (infer `false` only when there is genuinely nothing to offload — never key it off an installed plugin catalog, which silently disables the dispatched-task ledger guard); `deploy_target` **defaults to `n/a` and is never inferred** — a live surface exists only where the user names one, in the request or in reply to the card, and deploy-shaped signals in the repo are not that naming; `cleanup_on_finish` true; `use_worktree` false; `integration_branch` from the epic plan, else the current mainline, else `main` — print it as `unknown` rather than dropping it; `model_plan` is mechanical, never invented or recalled from memory: the orchestrator tier is the detected session model, and every other tier (implementor, senior-implementor, researcher, test-runner, auditor, critic) is read verbatim from that role's `model:` + `effort:` frontmatter in the rendered role files — `agents/*.md` in this repo, or `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/*.md` for an installed run. A plan whose `model_plan:` lacks a role's tier, written before the role existed, is not refused; that role runs at its role file's `model:`.
4. **Derive the walk requirement.** From the declared surface flags: a surface an agent can open and drive → `walk: required`; nothing drivable → `walk: exempt`. It is recorded as plan-frontmatter `walk:`. **Exemptions derive from declared configuration and are approved with the configuration, never invented mid-run** — there is no mid-run `n/a`, and the Verify gate reads an absent or unrecognized key as `required`, so an omission never becomes an exemption.
5. **Derive the Verification Matrix.** One row per acceptance criterion. Tier defaults: user-visible behavior → **T3**; engine-divergent → **T2 both engines** plus **T3** for the user-visible AC; pure substrate with no runtime surface → **T1/T2** with a one-line justification; perceptual fidelity → **T3**, T4 available; docs → **T0/none**. A criterion whose only evidence is a lifecycle artifact — a close-out report, `continuation.md`, an ADR — is a Step-9 checklist item, never a matrix row, and a process fact — that a step was walked, a reader dispatched, a check run — is never a T4 row: the matrix holds what the product does. It is a close-out obligation instead.
6. **Step 0 ends at its card.** Write every setting into the plan's frontmatter, `scale-recommendation: "<two sentences: why this scale for this ask>"` beside `scale:`, then put `card.sh step0 <plan>` whole: the configuration card, approved on its own reply before Step 1, the reply the evidence line's `via`.
7. **Create the task list on approval** — one task per planned step, `0:` marked completed — then go to Step 1.

**The `design-interview:` flag.** `design-interview: true | false` is standing Step-0 configuration, default `true`, recorded in plan frontmatter beside `walk:`. It is not derived from anything: `false` is the **standing Step-0 form** of Step 2's user-only interview waiver, carrying that waiver's whole force and none of it weakened — the run proceeds without the Design Interview because the user said so. A standing form is **not a second way to discharge that waiver**: the reason is still written verbatim into the design's assumptions, quoting the Step-0 reply, and the flag itself records with attribution — `design-interview: false <user> <date>`, the sibling literal of `design-waived:` and `rigor-override:`, because that attribution is the only trace that a human made the call. `design-interview:` is recorded, not validated — no hook parses it, unlike `walk:`, whose enum blocks at write time, and `rigor-override:`, whose presence the minimum checks read; **an agent never sets it**, in either direction, and a later reader meets a decision rather than an absent interview.

**The review fields.** Step 0 writes `review-cadence:`, `fix-policy:` and `fix-cap:` into the plan header beside `rigor:`, each with the value its rigor sets (the table in `SKILL.md`): `single` writes `once`, `S1,S2-on` and `2`; `double` writes `once`, `S1,S2-on` and `10%` of the plan's rows. Each is the user's to set with the Override DSL: `set fix-policy=<ratings>` takes `S1 S1-on S1-off S2 S2-on S2-off S3 S4`, comma-joined, `set fix-cap=<n>` takes a number, and `set review-cadence=once` names the one cadence there is. A value the user sets is read verbatim and never widened by an agent.

**The `permissions` line.** In bypass and auto mode an engaged run answers the platform's permission questions from each asker's workspace; in any other mode the platform's dialog reaches the user as before. Approving the card is the consent; `permission-answers: false` in `.bionic/config.yaml` turns it off.

**Task-list format — blessed, and it binds across every step, not just Step 0.**

- **Chronological order of execution.** The list reads top to bottom as the work will actually happen.
- **Format A — `<task>: <short desc>`** (e.g. `3: Plan — lock tasks and matrix`).
- **Format B — `<task>/<task>: <short desc>`**, only where tasks are involved (e.g. `4/2: fix the window conversion`).
- **A takes precedence over B when tasks are present**: the step's own entry is DROPPED and its tasks stand in its place. Never print `4: Implement` above `4/1: …` — display space is precious and the parent line is duplicative. It is also a line that can never complete until all its tasks do, so it carries no signal.
- **Short descriptions.** The subject is a signal, not a summary — detail belongs in the task body or the plan.
- **No filler.** Every entry is a real unit of work with a real status.
- **No freeform titles.** An entry without a `<task>:` or `<task>/<task>:` prefix is malformed.
- Mark `in_progress` on starting and `completed` the moment it is done — never batch completions. When a subagent finishes, the orchestrator updates the entry; dispatched work is ledgered in the plan, never as a bare task.

The list is the user's visible progress surface. No hook can read a task list, so the format is the whole discipline. The per-task expansion happens at plan approval; see Step 3.

**Override DSL.** `set <axis|flag>=<value>` and `set verify(<AC>)=<tier>`, comma-separated, ending in `confirm`. `explain [axis]` renders the axis tables and never counts as confirmation; a free-text question about the display is treated as `explain`, never as a parse error. A rigor override BELOW a derivable minimum is **accepted, never refused** — no code refuses it, and neither does this skill. Before locking, name the binding minimum, the evidence class it was buying ("double gives `evidence` its own reader; without it, one critic holds every question"), and what specifically is given up; then proceed with the user's value and record `rigor-override: <user> <date> derived=<v> chosen=<v>` in frontmatter, so every later reader sees a decision rather than a derivation error. The regression setting is the sibling: `session-poker.sh regression <yes|no> '<reply>'` writes `regression:` and, when the value differs from the scale default, records `regression-override: <user> <date> derived=<v> chosen=<v>` in frontmatter. The minimum checks read the rigor marker and log `user-overridden` instead of a violation. Advisory strength scales with the minimum's reason — the security/privacy flag minimum gets the strongest language here — but there are **no carve-outs**: every minimum accepts the override.

**Evidence:** `Step 0: configured at <ISO> via <reply>; model_plan=<tiers>`
